title: Audit local skills, hooks, and tutorial text for setup-specific assumptions
scope: Perform a bounded local-only audit of recent skills and hooks to identify assumptions tied to the author's machine, Obsidian vaults, pi-specific worker dispatch, Codex config/profile snippets, ketch/web-discovery setup, destructive-guard behavior, agent-python-like setup, and bash alias setup. goals: Map the local tutorial artifacts that matter for the six focus items.
Identify concrete setup-specific assumptions and likely out-of-date claims, marking each as local-evidence-only until T003 verifies freshness.
Assess whether hooks/destructive-guard behavior, especially the Obsidian guard, is general-user-safe or requires opt-in/setup explanation.

non_goals: Do not read any tmp/ or archive/ directory.
Do not edit skills, hooks, recommendations, README, references, or reports.
Do not make freshness claims about external tools without T003 evidence.
Do not run Python unless you first read the shared agent-python README required by project instructions.
safety: Follow /home/abhmul/Documents/ai-tools-intro/AGENTS.md: newcomers audience, plain language, neutral factual tone, no hype or emoji.
Treat user-provided claims as unverified; record them as candidates for verification rather than facts.
If reading ~/.bash_aliases, extract only aliases/functions relevant to ai-tool harness setup and omit secrets, tokens, unrelated paths, and private machine details.
success_criteria: The handoff addresses all six focus items and distinguishes direct local evidence from unverified assumptions.
The handoff lists any recommended edits or setup sections by target file/path without applying them.
No forbidden directories or prompt-buffer.md were read.
